target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```

vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
```

target.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls would never trigger the
no-progress circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls.
This happens commonly with SSH timeouts, Docker connection-refused errors, and
other transient failures where timestamps or session ids in the error message
change each time while the actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts:196-246` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips volatile text but preserves `{status,exitCode,timedOut,failureKind,exitSignal}` with numeric signal normalization via `normalizeExitSignal()` |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts:670-806` | Restore `date` test (warning), upgrade `flaky-helper` (critical/breaker), add `distinct failure kinds` + `distinct exitSignal values` tests |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` | **Runtime proof** — direct tsx execution through production code path (no vitest mocks), shows subsystem logger output |

## Why This Change Was Made

Split `hashExecToolOutcome` so `failed` exec results are hashed without the
volatile output text, while `completed` exec results keep output in the hash
as a real progress signal. A failed command producing different error strings
across identical retries should still count as no-progress.

## User Impact

Stuck agents that loop retrying the same failed `exec` call now correctly hit
the global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway
sessions instead of burning tokens forever.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof (direct Node.js, no vitest)

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` exercises the fix through the
**production `detectToolCallLoop` code path** using `tsx` — no vitest, no mocks.
The test bypasses vitest's module isolation and verifies the real subsystem
logger output.

**Real environment:**
- OS: Linux x86_64, kernel 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node.js v24.13.1, tsx v4.22.3
- Commit: `204c3bd9`

**Exact command:**

```
$ /path/to/tsx src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Full terminal output:**

```
=== Real runtime proof: failed-exec loop detection (#93917) ===

Prove 1: Repeated docker-ps failures (same failureKind, varying error text)
[agents/loop-detection] Global circuit breaker triggered: exec repeated 30 times with no progress
  stuck=true  level=critical  detector=global_circuit_breaker
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — circuit breaker triggered

Prove 2: Repeated date calls (completed, varying output)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — varying completed output stays at warning

Prove 3: Mixed failure kinds (timeout/terminated/connection_refused)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — distinct failure modes not merged

Prove 4: Numeric exitSignal (9=SIGKILL) vs string (SIGTERM)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — numeric and string exitSignals kept distinct

=== All runtime proofs complete ===
```

**Observed result after fix:**
- Failed exec with same failureKind + exitCode now fires `global_circuit_breaker` ✅
- Completed exec with varying output stays at `warning` (output IS progress) ✅
- Different failureKind values produce distinct hashes — no false merge ✅
- Numeric exitSignal (9) and string exitSignal ("SIGTERM") produce distinct hashes ✅
- The `[agents/loop-detection]` subsystem logger confirms real production code path

### Unit tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts --reporter=verbose

```

change is pure hash computation; coverage for non-exec tool types is unchanged.

target.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Telegram senders could keep abandoned HTTP transports alive when the Telegram client options cache evicted old account/network entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache entry now retains the transport created for its client fetch so eviction can release the old dispatcher lifecycle instead of only deleting the client options object. Evicted entries are retired immediately, but their transport is closed only after active send-level leases finish, so cache pressure does not abort an in-flight Telegram send.

## User Impact

Operators running Telegram channels with many account or network option combinations should see stale Telegram transports released after cache eviction instead of accumulating idle connections over time, without changing existing Telegram send behavior for active requests.

## Evidence

- `env OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm --dir "$TASK_WORKTREE" exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/send.proxy.test.ts --hookTimeout=300000 --maxWorkers=1` — 1 file passed, 7 tests passed. The regressions drive 65 production-mode cache entries, verify the evicted transport `close()` is called, and verify eviction defers `close()` until the active send finishes.
- `pnpm --dir "$TASK_WORKTREE" tsgo:test:extensions` — passed extension test type checking.
- `OPENCLAW_DEV_AUTO_PAIR=false start_openclaw_dev_gateway.sh` — isolated OpenClaw dev gateway reached ready; the startup log recorded `http server listening` and `ready`.

Before the fix, the eviction regression failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the evicted transport close spy. The lease regression covers the active-send case that would be unsafe if eviction closed the transport immediately.

Running `openclaw exec-policy show` or `openclaw approvals get` to inspect effective exec policy shows config + host approvals state, but **not** per-session `/exec` overrides set in an active chat or cron session. Nothing in the CLI output or docs mentioned this gap. A user who had set `/exec security=full ask=off` in a session and then ran `exec-policy show` would see a different policy than what was actually in use, with no hint about why.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Both `exec-policy show` and `approvals get` build output from the config snapshot and host approvals file only — session state is never loaded in either path.

**Scope note:** this PR is a diagnostic clarification only. The underlying runtime issue — `SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED` despite effective policy showing `security=full` — is tracked separately in #79983 and requires a different fix path. Merging this should not close or de-prioritize that issue.

## User Impact

```
Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook, and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback sent `convertMarkdownTables(outboundText)` directly via `reply`, bypassing any channel sanitizer. Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners.

This adds `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

This matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

Nostr users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies on either outbound delivery or inbound DM replies. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — outbound adapter hook strips banner:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nostrPlugin } from "./extensions/nostr/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const result = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
```

**Inbound DM reply path — gateway harness strips banner before relay reply:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts --run -t "strips internal tool-trace"
```

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard container flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Signal setup required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also fixes setup/status gaps where Signal transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup now verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, so an account-list response alone is not treated as a working Signal setup.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup now verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output now exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is the command/test output and config transition coverage below.

target.title: fix(acp): skip oneshot sessions during startup identity reconcile
target.body:
Fixes #72013

## Summary

Gateway startup identity reconciliation attempts to resolve pending ACP session identities. Oneshot sessions are terminal by nature, but their identity often remains `pending` after completion. The reconcile loop tries to ensure a runtime handle for each one, which fails and produces misleading warnings:

```text
[gateway] acp startup identity reconcile (renderer=v1): checked=7 resolved=0 failed=7
```

This makes it look like ACP/Codex/Claude agent routing is broken when fresh sessions are healthy.

## Fix

Skip sessions with `mode === "oneshot"` in `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` so the startup scan only processes persistent sessions that may genuinely need identity resolution.

## Changed files

- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.ts` -- Added `session.acp.mode === "oneshot"` guard after the session key check
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.test.ts` -- Regression test: oneshot session with pending identity is skipped (checked=0, no ensure/getStatus calls)
- `scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts` -- Production-path proof: session-store-visible `listAcpSessionEntries` + reconcile eligibility

## Overlap with #85399

PR #85399 (bound startup sidecar fanout) rewrites the same startup reconcile loop. This PR's guard (`session.acp.mode === "oneshot" -> continue`) is an independent behavior concern from #85399's fanout bounding. Both changes apply cleanly on the same function. Landing order should not matter as long as the guard is preserved during any rebase.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Startup identity reconcile must not process store-visible oneshot ACP rows that still have pending identity + stable `acpxSessionId`, while persistent pending rows remain eligible.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node from workspace toolchain, OpenClaw PR branch `fix/acp-reconcile-skip-oneshot` at commit after proof script add, using **production** `listAcpSessionEntries` + `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` (not a reimplemented loop).
- **Why SQLite-only proof is insufficient:** `listAcpSessionEntries` joins SQLite `acp_sessions` rows to a readable session-store entry and **drops** rows without a matching store entry (`session-meta.ts`). This proof seeds **both** the JSON session store and SQLite via production `upsertAcpSessionMeta`, then prints direct list output.
- **Exact command run after this patch:**

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts
```

- **Evidence (redacted paths are machine temp dirs; no secrets):**

```console
PROOF_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj
STORE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/sessions/main.json
DATABASE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/state/openclaw.sqlite
LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:oneshot-proof-visible mode=oneshot state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=sess-oneshot-proof
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=eeeedc2b-ead9-40e5-b40e-71fa768ecf19
ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
RECONCILE_ELIGIBLE_CALL sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent
RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1 resolved=0 failed=0
ENSURE_CALLS=["agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible"]
ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true
PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true
PROOF_OK

```

Interpretation:
- `LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2` with both `ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` and `PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` shows the startup scan input path sees both rows (the ClawSweeper gap from SQLite-only injection).
- `RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1` with `ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true` and `PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true` shows oneshot is skipped while the persistent pending stable row remains reconcile-eligible.

## Tests

target.title: fix(slack): keep thread label snippet truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<!--
AI-assisted: generated with Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack thread labels injected into the agent prompt context could contain invalid Unicode when thread starter messages contain emoji near the 80-character snippet boundary.

When a Slack thread reply arrives, OpenClaw builds a human-readable label for the thread (e.g. `"Slack thread #general: Great idea about the 🚀 launch…"`) and injects it into the LLM's context. The snippet is produced by collapsing whitespace then calling `.slice(0, 80)`. Emoji and supplementary-plane characters are represented as two UTF-16 code units (a surrogate pair). If the cut point lands between the two halves, the result contains an isolated surrogate — invalid Unicode — which is then passed to the model as part of its context string.

This affects two sibling helper functions:
- `prepareSlackThreadContext` in `prepare-thread-context.ts` — builds `threadLabel` for live thread replies
- `resolveSlackAssistantRootThreadLabel` in `prepare-thread-context-root.ts` — builds the label for assistant-root thread sessions

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 80)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 80)` in both helpers. The surrounding `.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` and `.trim()` calls are unchanged; only the final truncation step is made surrogate-safe. `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` is the established helper for this pattern throughout the codebase.

Both sites are fixed in the same PR because they share the identical bug pattern and are tested together.

## User Impact

Slack users who start threads with emoji-rich messages long enough to reach the 80-character boundary (common in practice — a single sentence with a few emoji easily hits this) would cause the agent to receive a malformed thread label in its prompt context. This can produce garbled context, confuse the model about the thread subject, or trigger a rejected API call on providers that validate Unicode input. After this fix, thread labels are always valid Unicode strings.

## Evidence

- **`prepare-thread-context.ts:228`** (pre-fix): `const snippet = starter.text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").slice(0, 80);` — `snippet` is used on the next line as `threadLabel = \`Slack thread ${params.roomLabel}: ${snippet}\``.
- **`prepare-thread-context-root.ts:111`** (pre-fix): `const snippet = params.starterText.replace(/\s+/g, " ").slice(0, 80).trim();` — `snippet` is returned as part of the label string `\`${base} (assistant root): ${snippet}\``.
- Both labels are consumed by downstream prompt-context builders and reach the LLM.
- **Fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 80)` — same length cap, surrogate-pair-safe.
- **Diff:** 5-line change across 2 files — two new imports, two call-site replacements; no logic change.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(codex): isolated cron reports Codex startup stalls
target.body:
Related #84567 and #64744.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where isolated cron runs routed through Codex could report a generic setup/startup timeout when Codex app-server startup had already reached the required `initialize` protocol request and then stalled. That made the user-visible failure look like `isolated agent setup timed out before runner start` instead of identifying the Codex initialize phase that owned the blocked startup.

The reporter path is #84567's isolated cron setup-timeout route for `openai/gpt-5.5` / Codex routing. #64744 provides the older Codex initialize-hang context. This PR does not auto-close #84567 because a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn is still not claimed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the existing startup budget but carries the remaining deadline into the Codex app-server client startup owner, where it is consumed only around `client.initialize()`. That lets `codex app-server initialize timed out` win once startup has reached `initialize`, while pre-initialize factory/start-context hangs still use the generic startup timeout path.

This conflict-resolution update rebases the PR onto current `origin/main` and adapts the original deadline wiring to main's current `shared-client.ts` factory-options contract. It intentionally preserves main's removal of `client-factory.ts` and does not reintroduce the older active-lease notification hook that no longer exists on the current client contract.

Out of scope: OAuth profile selection, provider/model routing, successful Codex app-server startup behavior, post-`thread/start` turn execution, user config, schema, protocol payloads, public APIs, and any claim that the reporter's live/idle worker snapshot alone proves the exact stall was inside `client.initialize()`.

## User Impact

Codex startup attempts that reach `initialize` and then stall now fail at the initialize lifecycle boundary with a more specific diagnostic, instead of being masked by the broader startup watchdog. Operators and maintainers get clearer failure attribution for isolated cron Codex startup stalls before `thread/start`.

The highest-risk area is Codex app-server startup availability, because timeout ordering and connection-closed retry ownership change around the first protocol request. The mitigation is narrow: callers that omit the internal initialize deadline keep the previous factory-wide timeout behavior, and retries stop only after the outer startup watchdog has already abandoned startup.

## Evidence

Earlier proof retained from the PR:

- Real-stdio stalled initialize proof: a spawned Codex app-server child received the real `initialize` request, did not answer, and OpenClaw raised `codex app-server initialize timed out` rather than the generic startup timeout. This proof uses a deterministic real-stdio stalled app-server child, not reporter-only OAuth credentials.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538

target.title: fix(cli): proxy run signal handling + clone into existing-empty git checkout dir
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw proxy run -- <cmd>` ignores SIGINT/SIGTERM: the child process is orphaned on Ctrl+C, the proxy server is never stopped, and the capture session is never ended. A signal landing during server startup (before the child spawns) is lost entirely. Separately, `ensureGitCheckout` fails when `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` points at an existing empty directory, because `git clone <url> <dir>` runs with `cwd: <dir>`.
- Why it matters: orphaned children keep ports/resources held after the CLI exits, and capture sessions are left dangling in the store; the update path errors out on a perfectly valid empty checkout dir.
- What changed: `runDebugProxyRunCommand` registers SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers before any await, forwards the signal to the child, remembers a signal that lands mid-startup (`pendingSignal`) and applies it to the just-spawned child, and funnels all cleanup through one idempotent `shutdown()` that stops the server, ends the session, and exits with the child's code. `ensureGitCheckout` clones into `"."` with `cwd` set to the target dir.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): `proxy start` signal handling, the capture store API, proxy validation output, and all other update-cli steps are untouched.

- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` — 182 passed, including a new test asserting the clone into an existing empty `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` uses `.` as the destination.

target.title: fix(plugins): bound hosted catalog feed reads on non-streaming responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readHostedCatalogResponseText` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts` used two read paths: the streaming branch incrementally enforced `maxBytes`, but the non-streaming branch called `response.text()` first and only checked the byte count afterward. That check-after-allocate pattern could OOM on oversized bodies when the response was not stream-backed or when `Content-Length` was missing or wrong.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route all hosted catalog feed reads through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper from `src/infra/http-body.ts`, reusing the same byte cap, idle timeout, and overflow error contract as other bounded HTTP reads. For stream-less fetch shapes, fail closed instead of trusting `Content-Length` before the shared helper's `arrayBuffer()` fallback. This deletes the duplicate streaming loop and the unsafe `response.text()` branch.

## User Impact

Normal hosted catalog loads are unchanged for stream-backed responses. Oversized feeds fail at the shared byte cap; stream-less feeds now fail closed with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable` instead of trusting `Content-Length` and risking a full-body allocation.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-streaming hosted catalog feed reads could allocate the full response body before enforcing `maxBytes`; stream-less oversized bodies could still buffer via `arrayBuffer()` fallback.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0, `node:http` loopback server on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
  ok: unbounded read pulled the full oversized feed (1572963 bytes)
  ok: rejected oversized hosted catalog feed
  ok: bounded error message present
  ok: streamless hosted feed with underreported content-length is rejected
  ok: streamless hosted feed never reaches arrayBuffer()

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds before buffering underreported bodies
 ✓ rejects oversized streaming hosted feeds incrementally
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds without content-length

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `loadHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries` rejects a ~1.5 MiB loopback feed at the 1 MiB cap with `hosted catalog feed exceeds 1048576 bytes`; stream-less responses are rejected with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable`; and the underreported `Content-Length` proof confirms that path never reaches `arrayBuffer()`.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawHub hosted catalog endpoints; proof used loopback fetch and mocked `fetchImpl` only.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs` (committed on branch)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests added in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — oversized hosted feeds error at the cap on stream-backed responses; stream-less hosted feeds are now rejected.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — hosted catalog feed reads now use one bounded HTTP reader and refuse stream-less remote responses.
- Highest-risk area: plugin catalog refresh / hosted feed fallback behavior on large but legitimate feeds.
- Mitigation: default cap remains 1 MiB; successful feeds are far below it; bundled fallback behavior is unchanged on overflow.

target.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getRecentSessionContent` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the session-memory extraction path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session-memory extraction now uses a bounded hybrid reader:
- For transcripts that fit under the 16 MiB cap, it streams lines newest-first through the shared `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` helper and stops before retaining a line that would cross the cap.
- For transcripts that exceed the cap, it reads only the trailing 16 MiB and drops the first partial JSONL line, so a single over-cap record is not materialized.

This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving recent session context.

## User Impact

Session-memory extraction now safely bounds oversized transcripts while still keeping the most recent messages available for context.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests covering:
  - a transcript exceeding the cap with recent trailing messages — asserts the recent messages are preserved and the huge early message is absent,
  - a single JSONL row larger than the cap — asserts `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run` passes (5/5 tests).

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises both the oversized-tail path and the lone over-cap row path.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101475.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101475.mjs

Result contains recent user message: true
Result contains recent assistant message: true
Result does NOT contain huge early message: true

Result is null: true
```

The helper bounds reads for both pathological layouts without buffering the entire transcript into memory.

target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution already emits diagnostics when a configured SecretRef fails and provider env credentials are used instead, but `openclaw security audit` and doctor did not surface that boundary drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a config-layer plugin load path collector that reuses existing discovery and doctor bundled-path helpers, then maps results to structured security audit findings (`plugins.load_paths.*`). Added a shared secrets diagnostic helper (`collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics`) used by both security audit (`secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`) and a new doctor health check (`core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`). Deep skill code-safety scan retains `includeArchived: true`.

## User Impact

* Operators running `openclaw security audit` now get early warnings when `plugins.load.paths` points at risky or missing locations, and when configured SecretRefs silently fall back to env credentials.
* `openclaw doctor` now emits structured warnings for SecretRef env fallback cases that previously only appeared in runtime/gateway logs.
* No config schema, runtime enforcement, or secret resolution behavior changes.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts \
  src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts \

```

target.title: Add local Claw feed planning
target.body:
## Summary

Stacked after #101328. This adds the first read-only Claw feed layer so OpenClaw can discover a Claw from a feed entry and build the same lifecycle plan introduced in PR2.

- adds `openclaw.clawFeed.v1` types, strict parsing, and local feed file reading
- resolves feed entries to local Claw manifest sources with source-locality checks
- adds owner/trust metadata on feed entries and warnings for missing owner evidence
- adds `openclaw claws feed inspect <feed>` and `openclaw claws feed plan <feed> <claw>`
- keeps PR3 read-only: remote feed fetch, install, mutation, and ClawHub publish/search stay deferred

## Safety / ownership behavior

- relative feed sources must stay under the feed file directory
- absolute local paths are rejected
- remote `http`/`https` sources are rejected in this PR
- `file:` URLs are accepted only if they resolve under the feed directory
- feed entry id must match the resolved manifest id
- feed entry version mismatch is diagnostic-only warning so feeds can surface drift without mutating anything

target.title: docs(cli): clarify that exec-policy show and approvals get exclude per-session /exec overrides
target.body:
<!-- PR TITLE -->
docs(cli): clarify that exec-policy show and approvals get exclude per-session /exec overrides

<!-- PR BODY -->

## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw exec-policy show` or `openclaw approvals get` to inspect effective exec policy shows config + host approvals state, but **not** per-session `/exec` overrides set in an active chat or cron session. Nothing in the CLI output or docs mentioned this gap. A user who had set `/exec security=full ask=off` in a session and then ran `exec-policy show` would see a different policy than what was actually in use, with no hint about why.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Both `exec-policy show` and `approvals get` build output from the config snapshot and host approvals file only — session state is never loaded in either path.
- The existing `effectivePolicy.note` field is already rendered in both human-readable and `--json` output, so appending the caveat there is the minimal correct fix with no new surface.
- `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md`, `docs/cli/approvals.md`, and `docs/tools/permission-modes.md` all describe these commands without mentioning the session override gap; a `<Note>` block in each keeps the docs aligned with CLI output.

**Scope note:** this PR is a diagnostic clarification only. The underlying runtime issue — `SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED` despite effective policy showing `security=full` — is tracked separately in #79983 and requires a different fix path. Merging this should not close or de-prioritize that issue.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw exec-policy show` or `openclaw approvals get` now see the following appended to the policy note in both text and `--json` output:

```
Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

Docs pages for exec approvals, approvals CLI, and permission modes carry a matching `<Note>` block.

No config, approval logic, or enforcement behavior is changed. No migration required.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts`
  - `Test Files  2 passed (2)`
  - `Tests  30 passed (30)`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:**
  CLI diagnostics for `exec-policy show` and `approvals get` now warn that per-session `/exec` overrides are excluded, and docs match that caveat.

- **Real environment tested:**
  Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with fresh temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, rebased on latest `upstream/main`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$tmpdir"

pnpm openclaw exec-policy preset yolo --json
pnpm openclaw exec-policy show --json
pnpm openclaw approvals get --json
pnpm openclaw approvals get
```

Session inspection path reference (no live chat required):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.exec-hint.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

`exec-policy show --json` / `approvals get --json` note excerpt:

```text
Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

`approvals get` text excerpt:

```text
Precedence: Effective exec policy is the host approvals file intersected with requested tools.exec policy. Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

Session-status hint contract (Vitest):

```text
Current session exec defaults: host=gateway security=full ask=always node=worker-1.
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  Both CLI commands append the session caveat in JSON and text output; docs carry matching `<Note>` blocks; focused CLI tests pass.

- **What was not tested:**
  No live chat `/exec` command in Telegram/Discord; no committed proof scripts.

target.title: fix(session-fork): add timeout to parent-fork token count resolution (#101718)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveParentForkTokenCount` reads the parent session transcript file to estimate token count when forking a session, but has no timeout. On large transcripts (hundreds of MB) or slow filesystems (NFS, FUSE), this blocks session creation indefinitely, accumulating blocked async contexts that exhaust gateway connection slots (#101718).

## Why This Change Was Made

A 2-second `Promise.race` timeout is added in `resolveParentForkTokenCount`. On timeout, it returns `undefined` — the same sentinel the normal fallback path already produces. `resolveParentForkDecision` already handles `undefined` correctly: returns `{status: "fork"}` without a `parentTokens` estimate.

The existing fast paths (`resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens`, `cachedTokens`) are synchronous and complete before the timeout can fire. The timeout only guards the slow filesystem probe (`fs.stat` + transcript read up to 1MB).

Risk note: this touches the session-fork path used by gateway session creation and reply subagent spawn. The timeout default (allow fork without token estimate) is the safe choice vs blocking indefinitely.

## Evidence

### Layer 1 — 实机行为（聚焦测试终端输出）

```
 ✓ forkSessionEntryFromParent > forks transcripts in the directory for the store being mutated  165ms
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > returns fork with token count when the runtime resolves quickly    1ms
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > returns fork without parentTokens when the runtime hangs (timeout) 2008ms
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > returns skip when parent is too large                              1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The timeout test took exactly 2008ms, confirming the 2-second deadline fires and fork proceeds without blocking.

### Layer 2 — 相关测试套件

```
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts         → 4 passed ✓
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.test.ts → (existing tests) ✓
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts -t "fork"    → (existing tests) ✓
```

### Layer 3 — 静态检查

```
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 82ms on 2 files using 1 threads.
```

### Changes

| File | + | - | Net |
|------|---|---|-----|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts` | +7 | -1 | +6 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts` | +50 | -1 | +49 |

Closes #101718.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook, and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback sent `convertMarkdownTables(outboundText)` directly via `reply`, bypassing any channel sanitizer. Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners.

This adds `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

This matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

Nostr users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies on either outbound delivery or inbound DM replies. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — outbound adapter hook strips banner:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nostrPlugin } from "./extensions/nostr/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const result = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
```

**Inbound DM reply path — gateway harness strips banner before relay reply:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts --run -t "strips internal tool-trace"

 ✓ nostr inbound gateway path
   ✓ strips internal tool-trace banners before inbound DM replies

      Tests  1 passed | 2 skipped (3)
```

The test drives the real gateway `onMessage` → `deliver` callback boundary and asserts the relay `reply` receives `converted:Done.` (sanitized before `convertMarkdownTables`), not the raw tool-trace banner.

**Outbound adapter regression:**

```

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

target.title: fix(acp): skip oneshot sessions during startup identity reconcile
target.body:
Fixes #72013

## Summary

Gateway startup identity reconciliation attempts to resolve pending ACP session identities. Oneshot sessions are terminal by nature, but their identity often remains `pending` after completion. The reconcile loop tries to ensure a runtime handle for each one, which fails and produces misleading warnings:

```text
[gateway] acp startup identity reconcile (renderer=v1): checked=7 resolved=0 failed=7
```

This makes it look like ACP/Codex/Claude agent routing is broken when fresh sessions are healthy.

## Fix

Skip sessions with `mode === "oneshot"` in `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` so the startup scan only processes persistent sessions that may genuinely need identity resolution.

## Changed files

- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.ts` -- Added `session.acp.mode === "oneshot"` guard after the session key check
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.test.ts` -- Regression test: oneshot session with pending identity is skipped (checked=0, no ensure/getStatus calls)
- `scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts` -- Production-path proof: session-store-visible `listAcpSessionEntries` + reconcile eligibility

## Overlap with #85399

PR #85399 (bound startup sidecar fanout) rewrites the same startup reconcile loop. This PR's guard (`session.acp.mode === "oneshot" -> continue`) is an independent behavior concern from #85399's fanout bounding. Both changes apply cleanly on the same function. Landing order should not matter as long as the guard is preserved during any rebase.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Startup identity reconcile must not process store-visible oneshot ACP rows that still have pending identity + stable `acpxSessionId`, while persistent pending rows remain eligible.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node from workspace toolchain, OpenClaw PR branch `fix/acp-reconcile-skip-oneshot` at commit after proof script add, using **production** `listAcpSessionEntries` + `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` (not a reimplemented loop).

target.title: fix(telegram): cap warnedInvalidEntries warn-once Set via createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in the Telegram `warnedInvalidEntries` Set — every distinct invalid `allowFrom` entry (non-numeric Telegram user IDs like `@username` or arbitrary strings) would grow the Set without bound.


## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime`, matching the existing pattern in `bot-updates.ts`.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4 096 distinct invalid entries. Beyond that cap, the oldest entries are evicted (LRU), and re-warning them is a benign nudge back to correct configuration.

## Evidence

Real-path proof — `normalizeAllowFrom` exercised with `tsx` (no VITEST guard, warnings actually fire):

```text
$ node --import tsx extensions/telegram/proof-live.mjs

=== First call: 3 invalid entries trigger warnings ===
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@username" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "invalid!" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "notanumber" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["12345","67890"],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@username","invalid!","notanumber"]}

=== Second call: same invalid entries (dedup — no new warnings) ===
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":[],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@username","invalid!","notanumber"]}

=== Valid-only call: no warnings ===
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["11111","22222","33333"],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":[]}

=== Wildcard + invalid ===
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@bad" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["12345"],"hasWildcard":true,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@bad"]}

PROOF COMPLETE
```

- First call: 3 distinct invalid entries → 3 warnings emitted
- Second call: same entries → 0 new warnings (dedup works)
- New entry (`@bad`): 1 new warning emitted
- Valid numeric IDs and `tg:`/`telegram:` prefixes handled correctly

target.title: fix(codex): keep root memory in bootstrap context
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #94295.

Native Codex currently suppresses root workspace `MEMORY.md` when memory tools are available, causing `/context` to show the file as present but injected with `0` chars. That makes sparse bootstrap memory unavailable unless the model already knows to ask memory tools for the right fact.

This PR keeps root `MEMORY.md` in the bounded workspace bootstrap prompt context and leaves memory tools available for deeper recall.

## Changes

- Stop selecting root `MEMORY.md` as a tool-routed bootstrap file for native Codex turns.
- Stop filtering root `MEMORY.md` out of `buildBootstrapContextForFiles(...)` when memory tools are present.
- Stop excluding root memory from Codex prompt-context selection.
- Update Codex app-server tests to expect nonzero `MEMORY.md` injection unless normal bootstrap budget truncation applies.
- Update the Codex harness reference, Codex harness runtime, token-use, and system-prompt docs for the new native Codex `MEMORY.md` default.

## Why

`MEMORY.md` is the sparse long-term bootstrap memory surface. It can contain ambient operating facts that the model needs before it can know which memory query to run. Tool-based recall is useful, but it should not replace bootstrap memory by default.

Related broader routing work: #83612. This PR is intentionally narrower and addresses the direct `MEMORY.md injected 0 chars` regression.

## Validation

Focused local validation on the Raspberry Pi checkout at `385b6f50a17a62555ce1abd30c28c9c9b8fa2978`:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-attempt-support.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-attempt.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "keeps MEMORY.md in bounded context"
git diff --check
rg -n 'not pasted into every native Codex|not pasted into native Codex|do not paste raw `MEMORY\.md`|workspace-memory note|read on demand through memory tools|tool-routed `MEMORY\.md`|MEMORY\.md` pointers|fallback injection' docs/concepts/system-prompt.md docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference.md docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime.md docs/reference/token-use.md || true
```

Results:

- `attempt-context.test.ts`: 4 passed.
- Focused `run-attempt.test.ts` memory case: 1 passed, 104 skipped by `-t`.
- `git diff --check`: no output.
- Stale-doc wording scan: no output.

## Real behavior proof

**After-fix real behavior proof from Nick's Raspberry Pi OpenClaw host:**

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Native Codex was suppressing root workspace `MEMORY.md` when memory tools were available, causing `/context` to show the file as present but injected with `0` chars. The fix keeps root `MEMORY.md` in the bounded workspace bootstrap prompt context while retaining memory tools for deeper recall.
- **Real environment tested:** Nick's real Raspberry Pi 5 OpenClaw host, running the installed OpenClaw package reported as `OpenClaw 2026.6.6 (8c802aa)`. The installed runtime bundle patched in-place was `/home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
openclaw --version
rg -n "MEMORY.md is injected|OpenClaw does not paste|memoryToolRoutedBootstrapFiles = \\[\\]|excludeMemory: false" \
  /home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js \
  /home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase/extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts
node --check /home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js
openclaw config validate
git -C /home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase diff --check -- \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Actual terminal output from the real OpenClaw host after patching:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.6.6 (8c802aa)

$ rg -n "MEMORY.md is injected|OpenClaw does not paste|memoryToolRoutedBootstrapFiles = \\[\\]|excludeMemory: false" \
  /home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js \
  /home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase/extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts
/home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase/extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts:207:      excludeMemory: false,
/home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase/extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts:762:    `MEMORY.md is injected through the bounded workspace context when present. Use ${toolNames.join(" or ")} for deeper durable memory beyond the injected bootstrap context.`,
/home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js:274:        const memoryToolRoutedBootstrapFiles = [];
/home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js:286:          excludeMemory: false,
/home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js:630:        `MEMORY.md is injected through the bounded workspace context when present. Use ${(params.toolNames?.length ? params.toolNames : Array.from(CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES)).join(" or ")} for deeper durable memory beyond the injected bootstrap context.`,

$ node --check /home/rpiuser_nick/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-attempt-BtRhrKv-.js
# no output, exit 0

$ openclaw config validate
Config valid: $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json

$ git -C /home/rpiuser_nick/projects/active/openclaw-pr81185-rebase diff --check -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts
# no output, exit 0
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The installed native Codex runtime path no longer contains the suppressing `OpenClaw does not paste` behavior, no longer filters root `MEMORY.md` out of prompt context when memory tools are available, and now routes `MEMORY.md` through normal bounded bootstrap context (`excludeMemory: false`) while keeping memory tools available for deeper recall.


- **What was not tested:** A restarted-production-Gateway live `/context` screenshot or transcript was not captured in this PR body because Gateway restarts are held behind the normal operator approval gate. The after-fix evidence above covers the patched native Codex runtime path and validation commands on the real Pi host.

Hosted proof gate previously passed on the updated PR with: `External PR includes after-fix real behavior proof.`

## Maintainer note

target.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getRecentSessionContent` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the session-memory extraction path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session-memory extraction now uses a bounded hybrid reader:
- For transcripts that fit under the 16 MiB cap, it streams lines newest-first through the shared `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` helper and stops before retaining a line that would cross the cap.
- For transcripts that exceed the cap, it reads only the trailing 16 MiB and drops the first partial JSONL line, so a single over-cap record is not materialized.

This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving recent session context.

## User Impact

Session-memory extraction now safely bounds oversized transcripts while still keeping the most recent messages available for context.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests covering:
  - a transcript exceeding the cap with recent trailing messages — asserts the recent messages are preserved and the huge early message is absent,
  - a single JSONL row larger than the cap — asserts `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run` passes (5/5 tests).

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises both the oversized-tail path and the lone over-cap row path.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101475.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101475.mjs
=== Case 1: oversized transcript with recent tail ===
File size: 17826089 bytes (cap is 16777216 bytes)
Result contains recent user message: true
Result contains recent assistant message: true
Result does NOT contain huge early message: true
Result length under cap: true

=== Case 2: lone over-cap JSONL row ===
Result is null: true
```

The helper bounds reads for both pathological layouts without buffering the entire transcript into memory.

## Summary

target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, the exposure matrix flagged elevated and runtime/filesystem tools but did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`).

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit did not evaluate native command surfaces separately, name affected channels in finding detail, or warn when enabled extension plugins register commands reachable on those surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Control-plane exposure:** `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` now probes `cron` and `gateway`. Emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` (critical) when open inbound policy can reach control-plane tools.

**Plugin command surface audit:** `collectPluginsTrustFindings()` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()` and new/updated findings:

| checkId | After |
|---|---|
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | critical when native commands **or** skill commands enabled without `plugins.allow`; detail names channels |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | warn when enabled extensions register commands and native commands are configured |

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` uses the correct `plugins.allow` config key.

## User Impact

* Operators get clearer findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
* `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` when native commands are active without `plugins.allow`.
* No runtime behavior change.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Open inbound policy could expose gateway/cron control-plane tools and plugin command surfaces without dedicated audit findings.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `codex/audit-plugin-command-control-surface` (single commit on latest `main`).

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and `live:matrix` adapter.
- Converts all 81 former adapter-executed Matrix definitions from `execution.kind: transport` to ordinary QA Lab flows with explicit named QA Lab fixtures.
- Removes the adapter `runScenario` API, Matrix scenario-id dispatcher, adapter-owned retry policy, and adapter-owned timeout policy.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab. The Matrix adapter owns only live transport lifecycle/setup and transport primitives.
- Preserves the historical 94-ID migration ledger while attaching every legacy behavior to an existing QA Lab scenario. The 11 cases previously marked retired now also have runnable QA Lab scenario definitions.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Dependency/base proof:
